name: Cedar Breaks National Monument
story: Cedar Breaks National Monument is a natural amphitheater located in Utah, USA, near Cedar City. Established in 1933, the monument stretches across 3 miles with a depth of over 2,000 feet. It features high-altitude forests, subalpine meadows, and bristlecone pines that can be more than 1600 years old.
matters: The monument area forms the headwaters of Mammoth Creek, a tributary of the Sevier River. It covers the west side of the Markagunt Plateau, sharing geological connections with nearby Zion National Park.
